messages:
Maria C.: Heads up — got a customer checklist for their FedRAMP-style ask: they want cryptographic proof that audit logs are untampered and available for 3 years. What are the minimum telemetry + signing guarantees we can offer?

Aj P.: For signing we can do HMAC with KMS-wrapped keys today. We need to confirm rotation semantics and whether the signature covers the whole event or just a digest.

Samir R.: We currently emit audit events to Kafka + S3 export. Option A: sign at emit time before enqueue. Option B: sign when writing to long-term storage. A has stronger tamper protection but more perf cost.

Amy P.: Customer will require SLA around availability of evidence bundle delivery (they referenced 99.9% retrieval SLA). Also they want proof-of-delivery to a customer-managed SIEM endpoint.

Maria C.: Are there any constraints from Legal about handing over signed bundles to customers? @Legal any red flags around keys or signatures being shared?

Legal: We prefer not to export private keys. Signed event bundles are fine if signatures are verifiable (public key or key id + signing algorithm). Need documented verification instructions and authenticity metadata. No sharing of HSM internals.

Samir R.: Technical note: we can publish a per-tenant signing public key via our key registry endpoint, rotate keys with overlap window, and include key_id + signature in the event envelope. Example envelope snippet:```{"event_id":"e-123","payload_digest":"sha256:...","key_id":"kp-2026-04","sig":"base64..."}```

Aj P.: That works. Couple follow-ups: 1) key rotation policy (N days overlap), 2) replay/ordering protection — do we need append-only sequence numbers or Merkle tree roots for cross-checks?

Maria C.: Customer asked for non-repudiation and cross-tenant isolation. They specifically mentioned wanting sampling proofs (random subset) that we can reproduce.

Amy P.: On availability — we should clarify what "delivery" means. Do they want push to their SIEM, or downloadable audit bundles from our console? Both have different SLOs.

Samir R.: Implementation idea: 1) sign events at emit-time, 2) write to immutable S3 prefix with versioned objects, 3) compute periodic Merkle root for a day's set and sign that root. That lets customers verify membership without sharing raw keys.

Aj P.: That also helps retention/compact proofs for long horizons. But bucket immutability and object lock may be required for compliance (WORM). Ops needs to confirm whether our storage tier supports ~3yr retention with object lock per tenant.

Amy P.: I'll loop in eng-infra to confirm WORM options. For customer push endpoints, we need retry/backoff policy and dead-lettering. Those failure modes might affect contract SLA credits.

Maria C.: On schema changes: customers want stable audit schema for mapping RBAC events (role changes, policy updates, key rotations). We should publish a schema versioning policy and a deprecation window.

Samir R.: Agreed — recommend semantic versioning for audit schema, with at least 90 days of overlap for parsers. Also include machine-readable change logs.

Legal: For contract language, customers will want: scope of events, retention period, proof format, rotation notice period, and remedies for loss of evidence. We can offer standard contract language but enterprise may push for explicit acceptance tests.

Maria C.: Acceptance tests — they want validation harness that can replay a subset and verify signatures + membership proofs. Can we provide a test bundle generator?

Samir R.: Yes — we can add a "audit-validation" tool that produces signed sample bundles and verification scripts. It should support both SHA256 HMAC and RSA/ECDSA proofs depending on customer choice.

Aj P.: Security question: if customers want customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key), does that change our signing flow? We'd sign with their key or we publish the digest for them to sign? Need threat modeling.

Maria C.: Customer-managed KMS is an ask for some regulated customers. Two modes: 1) we call their KMS (we don't hold private key), 2) we publish digest and they sign externally and re-ingest signature — latter increases complexity.

Legal: Option 1 is acceptable if we have contractual MSA for cross-account key access and audit trail proving we only call KMS for signing. Option 2 is also OK but has obvious operational overhead.

Amy P.: Operationally, calling external KMS could affect latency; fallback options needed. Also we need to log and audit those calls (KMS call success/failure events).

Samir R.: Vulnerability triage note: signing path must be hardened. Any CVE in crypto libs requires immediate assessment. Also need to ensure key ids in events don't leak useful material.

Aj P.: For RBAC changes: include both before/after state in events and record actor_id, request_id, and policy_version. Small, consistent field names help mapping to customer IAM.

Maria C.: Next steps: 1) draft minimal spec for signing + proof-of-membership (Samir), 2) storage immutability options (Amy), 3) contract language draft (Legal), 4) validation harness PoC (Aj). I'll compile and send to the customer by EOD Friday.

sec-bot: Deploy job #8272 succeeded to prod (audit-signer v0.9.1) :white_check_mark:

Samir R.: noted — will use that build for the PoC.

Maria C.: Thanks all. If anyone has blockers ping me directly. :thumbsup:
